title: Battle Arena Toshinden
description: Battle Arena Toshinden is a well-known Playstation 1 3D fighting game. It was one of the first games I bought for my PS1. It's a Tekken-style one-on-one fighting game that involves mostly hand-to-hand combat and combos. Apparently a DOS port was also made of the game, and it's better than you might think, although not the same as the PS1 version even though it shares the same characters, moves, and controls. The controls are certainly one of the trickier parts, since using the keyboard to move around in 3D while trying to remember what all of the attack / block / etc buttons do can be challenging! It runs a little slowly as well, no doubt due to doing all of its 3D work without the aid of a 3D accelerator card. An impressive technical achievement if nothing else! This demo version contains 3 characters from the full version: Eiji, Sofia, and Mondo. Apparently Earthworm Jim is also a playable character in the full version?!
multiplayer: Up to 2 players, Simultaneous shared keyboard competitive

title: Putt-Putt Goes to the Moon
description: Putt-Putt Goes to the Moon is an edutainment product in the "Junior Adventures" line that was popular in the 90's when it was first released, and continues to live on through re-releases on iOS, Android, and Steam. Your goal is to find the pieces to put together a space ship to send Putt-Putt back to Earth. Children can click around on many objects to see short animated clips play. Putt-Putt and the rest of the characters are fully voiced, so even kids who aren't strong readers yet will be able to play the game. This game seems like it would still be a lot of fun for kids with its colorful graphics and interaction.

title: Kosmonaut
description: Kosmonaut is in some ways the prototype of a more advanced game, Skyroads. The title screen even seems to say "Skyroads" in an elaborate font. The concept is a 3D "racing" game where the only goal is to reach the end of the course. You do so by controlling your speed and jumping at the right moments. The game is tough, mainly because when you crash or fall off the track, it mocks you and then you have to start over! But it's an interesting first concept that was developed more fully in later games. (We can also see how this game influenced modern games, such as Snail Mail for iPhone/iPad.)

title: Peter Pan: A Story Painting Adventure
description: Peter Pan: A Story Painting Adventure is a simple game aimed at young children. You control Peter Pan as he goes on an adventure and encounters a variety of different challenges. You interact by choosing an action that one of the four "Paintbox Pals" at the bottom of the screen suggests to help Peter get out of trouble. All of the actions are valid and will work, so there's not really any challenge to the game, it's more like a "Choose Your Own Adventure" where all of the options win. It might be fun for small kids because the production values are high. This demo provides an intro animated sequences with voiceover and a few scenes from the full game.

title: Drug Wars: A Game Based on the New York Drug Market
description: Written by a high school student and sometimes referred to as the "original GTA", the game has really nothing to do with Grand Theft Auto, and more to do with a stock market type simulation game that happens to have the theme of a drug dealer. In the game, you are given $2,000, and you need to buy and sell drugs to turn that into at least $5,500 to pay off your debt. As you move to different areas, time progresses, random events may occur, and the prices of the drugs changes. The game is presented in a distinct text mode system in monochrome, so you'll have to use your imagination. This game served as the inspiration for several other similar games, and was played by countless kids in high school IT labs back in the day.

title: Mortal Kombat 2
description: In terms of ports, DOS often received pretty terrible ones in the early days. (See for example Mega Man or Double Dragon for DOS ... or better yet, avoid them entirely.) However Mortal Kombat 2 is a surprisingly faithful rendition of the arcade classic game. Mortal Kombat is of course the supremely violent one-on-one fighting game series, famous for its Fatalities, violence, and unique combat system. This demo version only allows fights between Liu Kang and Reptile, however the full version features all 15 fighters. The graphics and sounds are relatively faithful to the arcade, and the game has the same feel, although of course using the keyboard to play will be nowhere near as satisfying as an arcade stick and buttons! (Note the keyboard controls below in the instructions.)
multiplayer: Up to 2 players, Simultaneous competitive deathmatch

title: Subhunt
publisher: Laboratory for Recreational Computing at the University of North Texas
description: Subhunt is an interesting submarine mission simulation game developed by a group at a university game development lab: Laboratory for Recreational Computing at the University of North Texas, which still exists today. Apparently it was coded entirely from scratch using no existing libraries in C++ and Assembly. Anyways, it's a submarine simulator, so there are lots of buttons and things to press, and you'll need to spend some time learning how everything works because this is not an arcade-type sim. It does provide you with a 3D-rendered view outside your sub. The full game contains 12 missions but only one is included in the shareware game.

title: Revenge of the Mutant Camels
description: A side-scrolling platforming shooting game from Jeff Minter's Llamasoft? It must be incredibly zany! With a name like Revenge of the Mutant Camels, that's pretty much a given. Here you pilot your goat riding a mutant camel as it runs from left to right, shooting in whichever direction you last moved, sorta like a Robotron / Llamatron platforming game. Things attack you from all angles and you try to retain your sanity as you try to shoot them. Graphics and sounds are also suitably zany. It's definitely an interesting experience but I personally didn't find it particularly fun to play!

It's a short adventure game using the typical Alone in the Dark engine so if you love the particular look of the original AITD game you'll enjoy the aesthetics of this adventure. The plot involves a tricker-treating kid who gets trapped in a bizarre and eerie toy store on Halloween. Fun to play albeit rather short, it was a free promo game after all.

title: Putt-Putt Joins the Parade
description: Putt-Putt Joins the Parade is the first in a long series of Putt-Putt games which are still being released over 20 years later. The game is an edutainment product in the "Junior Adventures" line that was popular in the 90's when it was first released, and continues to live on through re-releases on iOS, Android, and Steam. You play the titular car, Putt-Putt, who wants to join the parade. But first he must earn cash to pay for a car wash, among other assorted tasks. There are plenty of things for kids to click on which result in little animation / sound flourishes. The game is designed to use speech instead of text (good for younger players) so be sure to turn on your speakers.

title: Blackthorne
description: Although the character movement and general gameplay aesthetic may bear a strong resemblance to the classic Prince of Persia game, Blackthorne was actually developed by Blizzard Entertainment, who of course would later go on to create the wildly popular Warcraft, Starcraft, and Diablo series. In this demo version of Blackthorne you can get a taste of the full version of the game. It's an action-adventure game requiring excellent timing. The graphics and sounds are great, especially the smooth animations and stylistic world you explore. The dodging mechanic also works really well, although the complicated controls can take some getting used to. (Blizzard has made the full game available for free! Download the full version here.)

title: Colossal Cave Adventure
description: This is a bit before my time ... however, it's worth playing at least once, just to see one of the first text adventure games ever created. It was originally authored by Will Crowther in 1976, then expanded in 1977 with the help of Don Woods. In it you must type in commands to move through various locations and solve puzzles. This game inspired the ZORK series of games and thousands of others. (This is a 350 points version of the game. For lots more info on this game, plus dozens of other versions of the game for DOS and many other platforms, visit Baf's Interactive Fiction Guide: Adventure!)

title: Mortal Kombat 3
description: This demo pre-release version of Mortal Kombat 3 allows you to play as either Jax or Sheeva in a 1-player vs computer, or 2-player match. This is of course the third in the long-running series of MK games, known for their violent fatalities and signature gameplay which fighting game fans often either love or hate. This third installment looks and feels very similar to the arcade game, which is no small feat on MS-DOS in 1995. Although only two characters are playable here, you can get a feel for the game, including the characters' special moves. The main limitation to playing it in DOS is using the keyboard to play, with the default keys (arrow keys plus the Insert-Del-PgUp-PgDn keys as your attack keys) being rather difficult to use. Modern solutions like Joy2Key can help make this game easier to play. The full version is available from GOG.com in a set with games 1 & 2 of the series for a reasonable price.
multiplayer: Up to 2 players, Simultaneous shared keyboard competitive

title: Pea Shootin Pete
description: If you've played Spitwad Willy, you've played Pea Shootin' Pete. While I'm not entirely sure about the history of this game, it seems as though after Raoul Said created Spitwad Willy, he either licensed it to Pack Media Company under a new name, or rebranded it when be became involved somehow with the company. Anyways, other than that, it's pretty much the same game, and as such still borrows heavily from Pang (aka Buster Bros). title: Nethack
description: Despite it's name, this game does NOT involve any type of computer "hacking". It's actually my favorite "Roguelike" game, orignally based on the "Hack" roguelike. title: Tempest 2000
description: Tempest is a vector-based action / shooting arcade game that was released in 1981. Your ship rotates around the tubular playing field and shoots the enemies as they approach towards the screen. This updated version was released in 1994, with similar gameplay and a freshly updated design by Jeff Minter of Llamasoft fame. (It is known as one of the few good games released primarily for the Atari Jaguar system!) The graphics and sounds ratchet up the intensity level, with pixelated explosions and cycling colors complimenting the smooth vector-like animations. Safe to say that if you enjoyed the original you will like this updated version, presented here in demo form.

title: Blake Stone: Aliens of Gold
description: Not that bad at all. This is a game that Apogee released between Wolfenstein 3D and Rise of the Triad. Basically it uses the Wolfenstien engine with some modifications, the best of which is a map so you're not lost throughout the entire game. It also adds a greater variety of enemies, money which can be used to buy things, switches which change the level, and so on. It isn't quite as memorable as Wolf3D (mostly because it lacks the freshness of that game) but if you like the older 3D games like Wolf3D or Catacomb Abyss you might want to try it out. title: 3-Demon
description: 3-Demon is probably the strangest Pac-Man game you'll ever play. It is played in a first-person perspective, that is, in "3D". How does this work, you may be asking? Well it's kind of difficult to figure out where you're going, and where the ghosts are. Luckily there's sort of a radar at the bottom that tells you how close the ghosts are. Overall it's poor graphics and dated sounds don't detract much from the game, so it's probably unique enough to be worth checking out. Is this the first "3D shooting" game ever? Not really but it's still interesting!

title: Scorched Earth
description: The best tank war game I've ever seen. It's called 'The Mother of all games' by the author and was chosen as PC World magazine as the third best DOS game of all time. In it, you are competing against up to 10 other tanks (controlled by other players or by the computer) and you battle by entering a velocity and turret angle before firing off various weapons, which you can purchase between rounds. Your weapons available to buy include Nukes, Napalm, Smoke Tracers, and Liquid Dirt, among many others. It looks and plays great, and it's great fun blowing up a tiny little tank with a huge nuke. (There are several levels of computer AI available, however you generally choose from "dumb as a doornail" to "nearly perfect" ...) Video ReviewVideo review of Scorched Earth, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Ultima IV: Quest of the Avatar
description: Ultima IV: Quest of the Avatar is, unsurprisingly, the fourth in the famous and influential Ultima series of fantasy RPGs. In 1996 Computer Gaming World placed Ultima IV #2 on its "Best PC Games of All Time", and for good reason. Ultima 4 is considered a big step forward for the series, and for computer role-playing games in general. The world of Britannia is fleshed out more than the first three games and there is a lot more story and personality evident in the game and the world itself. Although the graphics are crude by today's standards, it's the gameplay of story, exploration, battles (using a great environmentally-aware battle system) and character customization that make the game a true classic. Worth playing for RPG fans, but take note that since it was made in 1987 this is a true hardcore old-school RPG with no hand holding that will take considerable effort to learn and get into! (Note that the full version of the game along with full manuals and other extras is available via GOG.com; free registration is required to download and play it.)

title: Zork: The Great Underground Empire
description: Zork: The Great Underground Empire is a seminal interactive fiction game, and the first in a series of influential text adventure games from Infocom. I don't often add interactive fiction games to the archive (see IF Archive for more of those) but I'll make exceptions for exceptional games! Originally released for the TRS-80 in 1980, the DOS port keeps the story and gameplay of the original game. (Most people probably remember playing it on DOS anyways!) This version is actually "Mini-Zork", described as a "Reader's Digest" version of the full game intended as a demo. It's described in the included readme thusly: "This program is a sample of the first Zork text adventure, published around 1981. The full game is available in the Lost Treasures of Infocom collection, volume 1, as well as in the Zork Anthology." Truly a classic of the genre!

description: If you're hunting for an enjoyable word game, this could be it. While I have never played "Boggle", this game looks lot like it. The premise is simple: you have three minutes to shift the letters around in a 5x5 grid and create as many words as possible. Points are awarded and the high scores are recorded. It would be a good idea to force players to look up words in the dictionary that they don't know, because I sometimes spelled words by accident while moving around the tiles! :)

title: Rags to Riches: The Financial Market Simulation
description: Rags to Riches is a simulation of being a stock broker, circa the early 90's. You start off with some cash, and you need to use your limited funds to buy investments and hire people to help you. By shrewdly investing, you can make lots of money and go on shopping trips to spend your $$$. This demo version gives you limited options (you can only hire a secretary and a pit runner) but you can get a taste of how the full game will play. (Tip: To hire your first employees, make sure J.E.A is selected on the Rolodex, then click the phone. Then click on the left sidebar to choose who you want to hire.)

title: William Shatner's Tekwar
description: William Shatner's Tekwar is a game based on the series of books written by Captain Kirk himself. Or rather the actor that played him I guess. I've never read any of the books, but if they're as bad as this game, I should be glad that I haven't. Although it uses the BUILD engine (the same engine used for Duke Nukem 3D and other games) this game plays very poorly. The graphics, while detailed, still manage to somehow look ugly. The gameplay is also head-scratchingly poor with no clear objectives and frustrating/cheap/stupid computer AI. If you're a fan of this genre of game, or Tekwar, you may want to take a look. But don't expect to play for long!

title: Mario & Luigi
description: Mario & Luigi is a clone of the popular Super Mario Bros game for the NES. The game has an interesting backstory, where the developer Mike Wiering made the game as a programming exercise, and a beta version somehow leaked out and even was taken and sold by another guy! (You can download this alternate version in the "extra files" area above.) The actual game, titled Mario & Luigi later released by Wiering (obviously with no official license from the "Big N") offers decent gameplay and six levels to complete. The engine was obviously re-used for later games such as Charlie the Duck, Sint Nicolaas, and the most obvious being Super Angelo! Anywho, this game is generally fun to play, and the executable is only 57k! (The Turbo Pascal 6.0/5.5 source code is available on the Wiering Software website as well.)

title: Rocks'n'Diamonds
description: Rocks'n'Diamonds is at its core a Boulderdash clone, but it's so much more than that! It comes with a huge collection of levels culled from other games; you get all of the levels from Boulderdash, Emerald Mine, Sokoban, and Supaplex. Plus it includes a level editor so you can create your own unique levels using any of the assets from those games. There also many additional levels available in case the hundreds that it comes with aren't enough! The graphics are well-drawn tiles at 800x600 resolution and the game includes MOD-style music as well. A great achievement and amazing amount of content available for free! (The game is continuing to receive updates, but only to the Windows and other more modern platforms: Recent versions of Rocks'n'Diamonds.)

title: Mice Maze
description: Mice Maze is plays very similarly to the Crusher and Crusher's Castle 2 games, also by Soleau Software. So if you've played those, you know what to expect here, except this time it's about mice and cheese, and cats on the prowl trying to kill you. If you haven't played the Crusher games, Mice Maze is a randomly generated puzzle / action game where you must discover the location of your lost mouse friend. The good part about randomly generated rooms is that the game is different each time you play. The bad is that the design will be, well, random, so some rooms will be very easy and others will be nearly impossible. Still it's decently fun to play and continues the mice theme that other Soleau games share. (Mice Moves and Mice Men.)

title: Baryon
description: Baryon is a little-known shoot-em-up, created by unknown South Korean developer ACRO Studio. The gameplay is similar to most vertically scrolling shooting games, but what sets this game apart is all of the crazy action going on. There's stuff blowing up left and right, along with a rocking Soundblaster soundtrack and some impressive graphical effects. (This game uses an obscure 256x200 video mode, perhaps to allow for all its graphical trickery?) There are different powerups available, as well as two different ships you can choose, each with its own abilities. The main problem with the game is that it's sometimes quite difficult to see the bullets and other things that will kill you. But it's an impressive looking game that's fun to play. Personally I die pretty quickly but if you're a shmup fan maybe you'll actually finish the first level ... there's only one level included in the shareware version. (Run GO.EXE to start the game.)

title: Happyland Adventures: X-mas Edition
description: This version of Happyland Adventures includes more of the platforming and collecting action that the original game provides, with a whole set of new winter / holiday themed levels. In fact this package includes both the Xmas levels and the original levels, as well as the map editor (Windows only) to create your own levels and play them. Just like the original version, in the Xmas Edition, the object is to collect happyland residents (little monster-guys). After you've collected and dropped off all of them (in the "happyzone"), you can exit the level. Happy graphics (thanks to the free SpriteLib library of free sprites by Ari Feldman) and happy sounds round out this solid package.

title: Freaks!
description: Freaks! is an interesting 3D-ish FPS game from the mid 90's. Released in 1994 (after the original Doom) Freaks! is a decent looking game with a weird mechanic: Your character moves forward and backward smoothly, but when turning, you turn instantly at 90 degree angles, making the game feel somewhere between a FPS and a turn-based first-person RPG. You shoot at enemies and hit them if they are directly in front of you. So it's gameplay is more basic than even Wolfenstein 3D. There is only a single weapon, and you don't collect any items or powerups as far as I know. It's a shame because it has some pretty great art, although a little bit gruesome for kids! The original author(s) made a new version available (along with the source code) which runs in Windows natively and has actual FPS turning, so check that out here: Freaks 2.x Windows Port

title: Bust-a-Move 2: Arcade Edition
description: Bust-a-Move (aka Puzzle Bobble) is an extremely popular series of bubble-matching games which combine a puzzle game's need for strategy with the quick-thinking and reflexes needed for success in an action game. It is popular in arcades as well as home consoles. This demo of Bust-a-Move 2 allows you to experience this conversion of the arcade game for DOS, albeit with no music and limited levels. The object is to shoot colored balls towards the top of the screen, aiming to match three or more to clear them from the board. You can also bounce 'em off the walls. Once the screen is clear, you move to the next board. Nice graphics and of course the loveable Bub & Bob from the Bubble Bobble games make an appearance.

title: Worms
description: This demo version of the popular WORMS game allows you to get a taste of what the full game is like. Patterned after older classics like Scorched Earth and, yes, even QBasic classic Gorillas, Worms allows you to control various militaristic worms which are trying to kill each other. You must judge angle, velocity, and wind as you fire weapons at each other. You can move your worms around, and use different weapons as you strategically battle each other (and destroy the landscape while you're at it.) It's quite cool, and has inspired a plethora of sequels over the years. Video ReviewVideo review of Worms, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Monster Bash
description: This is another of Apogee's EGA sidescrollers. This one is lesser known because it was a bit outdated when it was released ... VGA graphics were quickly becoming the norm by that time. However, while it IS a bit more linear than their previous games, it's still worth a look if you enjoyed Apogee's other EGA platformers. In this game you play a kid ("Johnny Dash") who is trying to rescue captured animals, and to do it, he must use his trusty slingshot to kill various undead and ... uh, alive enemies. Spooky! There are three difficulty settings so you should be able to get far even if you're no good at games. Check out the Monster Bash HD remake on GOG.com for the new and improved modern remake of this game! Video ReviewVideo review of Monster Bash, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: SLASH
description: SLASH is a variant of Nethack, one of the most popular old roguelike games. SLASH stands for "SuperLotsaAddedStuffHack" and true to its name (which may be a backronym) it adds a bunch of stuff and makes a bunch of changes. Based on v3.1.3 of Nethack, and including features from other hacks NetHack Plus and NetHack--, it adds roles, monsters, items, custom dungeon levels, and more. Worth a look if you like Nethack. If you don't like Nethack, don't bother with this!

title: Enchantasy: Quest For The Eternal Grimoire
description: Enchantasy seems to be a decent CRPG fantasy game, with the caveat that the author(s) REALLY want you to register this game. The story and environment seem pretty standard for this sort of game, with typical fantasy tropes. You walk around and use hotkeys to perform actions; thankfully the hotkeys are displayed on-screen at all times for easy reference. In the shareware version you are limited to saving your game 5 times. You can gain an additional 25 saves by noting the number the game provides when you go to save, visiting this archived page, and clicking on the number to get a 5-digit code for another 25 saves. Unfortunately the registered version seems to be unpreserved so all we'll get is the shareware game; use those saves wisely!

title: Corridor 7: Alien Invasion
description: This game was unfortunately released shortly after Doom, meaning that it had to compete with one of the best 3D shooters of all time using ... the Wolfenstein 3D engine. Not even a fair fight, really. While the game is decent enough, its pretty obvious that its using the Wolf3D engine, with its boxy environments and simple sprites. Overall, it has decent graphics (again, comparable to Wolf3D), and it could be enjoyable if you force yourself to forget about Doom and play this game based on its own merits.

title: Cosmo's Cosmic Adventure
description: Cosmo's Cosmic Adventure is one of Apogee's great EGA sidescrollers. Having been apparently abandoned by his parents, Cosmo must ... well, the story doesn't really matter here. This game plays similarly to Commander Keen, as you must platform your way through the levels. There is no world map here, you simply progress from one level to the next. One of the lesser-known Apogee classics, although the framerate is lower than other comparable games of the time (apparently due to the parallax scrolling). title: Beneath a Steel Sky
description: Originally a commercially released adventure game, Beneath a Steel Sky (BASS) was deemed freeware by Revolution Software in 2003. Now you can download and play it for free using the SCUMMVM software. This is a Lucasarts-style adventure game which takes place in a gritty, futuristic setting. Although the graphics and sounds are well done, some of the puzzles are a bit uninspired. Nevertheless it's clearly a well-made game and worth playing for adventure game fans. If you'd like a free pre-packaged version of the game that runs natively in Windows via the SCUMMVM engine (this is the full CD version) get the GOG.com version of Beneath a Steel Sky for free.

title: Star Control II: The Ur-Quan Masters
description: Star Control II is considered by many to be one of the greatest PC games of all time. (Even in 2018 it was voted as the top PC game ever in a large online poll.) The game is a space exploration / combat simulation with a deep story and a huge world to explore. There is a plethora of worlds to visit and quests to complete, along with an engaging plotline. Your interactions with various species allow you to form alliances which are important for completing the game. While most of the game is leisurely paced, combat turns into an action-packed experience. Definitely worth trying; this demo version gives you a taste of the full version experience. A free open-source Windows port of the full game, based on converted 3DO code released by the developers, is available here: The Ur-Quan Masters. Definitely recommended!NOTE: For the DEMO version of this game you will need to initially run it with DOSBox cycles set 1000! After the main game screen loads, you can increase the cycles to a more reasonable amount like 4000. Otherwise the game will appear too dark! (Press Ctrl-12 to increase the cycles while in-game.) More info Video ReviewVideo review of Star Control 2, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Warcraft: Orcs & Humans
description: This demo version of the full game gives you a taste of what the original entry into the Warcraft series of games was like. "Orcs & Humans" (or simply Warcraft I) came before Warcraft II and Warcraft 3 and while it has its merits, it is generally surpassed by later entries in the series in most ways. Still, it was the first real-time fantasy strategy game from Blizzard. This game will still be fun for fans of the genre, and those interested in the origins of their addiction since it served as the prototype for Blizzard's later more well-known games.

title: Crazy Drake
description: Crazy Drake is a duck / superhero who clearly is aspiring to be Earthworm Jim. The SNES / Genesis game starring an Earthworm (which was later ported to many other systems, even DOS!) was clearly an inspiration for this game. Crazy Drake moves much like Earthworm Jim, and like him has a gun with unlimited ammo. The levels have great graphics and nice animations. Again like Earthworm Jim, there are various entertaining gameplay elements scattered around, like riding balloons over a shark pit. The game controls generally well, and the music is repetitive but catchy. I hate to keep comparing the two, but they're so similar in style that if you like Earthworm Jim, you'll probably like this one too. (Note: When playing in-browser, the keyboard arrow keys may not work entirely correctly, ex trying to shoot up/left. If this is the case for you, try using the numeric keypad instead if your keyboard has one.)

title: Packman
description: Packman is, as its name suggests, an overt Pac-Man clone. The playing field is horizontal rather than vertical, and the colors are uglier than its arcade counterpart, but it plays competently enough, at least for a game distributed for free in 1983. As in the original game, you control "Packman" and gobble dots while avoiding ghosts. You can gobble a power pellet to turn the tables and eat the ghosts. You move slower while gobbling pellets. Don't expect any fancy features or arcade-accuracy but it's a game that some people will remember from their childhood.

title: Tetris Queen
description: Tetris Queen is a good game for people who enjoy Tetris, a great game for those who like the music of the band Queen (who doesn't?) and an absolutely fantastic game for those who like both. This game offers both classic mode (same as regular Tetris) and destroyer mode (Tetris "WITH BOMBS IN IT"). It also offers a two-player simultaneous mode, along with great graphics and music of some of Queen's greatest hits. description: Syndicate is a beloved classic DOS action / strategy game where you play a hit man for one of a handful of global corporations (syndicates) that have taken over the world. Reminiscent of the look of the X-Com games but in real-time, you move your squad of characters through the missions, earning money by successfully completing them to upgrade your team for the next mission. title: Ladder Man
description: Ladder Man is the first in a series of side-view puzzle games by Soleau Software. (The third game is available here: Ladder Man III. It seems like the second game was only available if you registered the first game.) Anyways this is a puzzle game where the object is to use your ladder, and push around various blocks, to collect all the diamonds and avoid anything that will kill you. Much like real life: Collect $, avoid dying. There are a variety of levels to choose from, and a visual tutorial that walks you through how the game works. The visuals are better in the sequel, but there is still plenty of content here for puzzle fans.

title: Aspetra
description: Aspetra is a console-style RPG in the veign of classic RPGs like Dragon Quest and the older Final Fantasy games. It clearly takes influence from those sort of games in terms of style and storytelling. The story involves wizards, political (village) intrigue, and other common fantasy game themes. Battles are turn-based and result from random encounters whenever you leave town. There are plenty of weapons, armor, and items to collect, as well as baddies to battle with. If you enjoy old-school console-style RPGs this one is a polished, if not particularly unique, addition to the genre.

title: Cavern of the Evil Wizard
description: If you've ever seen the Tom Hanks movie Big (1988) you'll probably remember a PC graphical adventure game that is shown briefly. It's identified as "Cavern of the Evil Wizard", but to the disappointment of many fans of the movie, it was just made up for the movie; it didn't actually exist. Now a developer has made his own interpretation of the game, based on the screens seen in the movie. It keeps the same CGA graphic aesthetic and text-based input. Although you know how the game ends, you'll now get to see how the hero got there! Very cool since I remember Googling this when I got the Internet long ago and being disappointed that it wasn't a real game. Well, here it is, the full game for your enjoyment! Thank you MontieMongoose! (A Windows executable is also included but running the DOS version is recommended by the author.) I recently learned that this game is an expansion of a previously developed game by BoMToons, so check out the archived site for some more history about it.

title: Joust VGA
description: Joust VGA is a clone of the famous Joust arcade game, which many other later games took as inspiration. (Perhaps most notably Balloon Fight on the NES.) The object is to ride your flying ostrich around the screen and joust the other riders off of their ostriches. The game plays quite well (although you may need to adjust the speed to avoid it playing super-fast) even though only the one-player mode is included in the shareware version. The graphics are faithful to the original and the game has a satisfying feel as you flap around and try to unseat the other riders.

description: Magic Carpet is a unique 3D experience. You play a mage who rides a magic carpet, and your goal in each level (50 in the full game, two in this demo) is to collect enough mana to fill your castle. You collect it via golden balls, and you'll also need to watch out for enemies such as giant worms and rival mages flying on their own carpets. The game is visually impressive and fluid, although with a short draw distance (lots of "fog"). This two-level demo gives you a taste of what the full game has to offer. title: Neut Tower
description: Neut Tower is a new MS-DOS game developed on actual 286 hardware and released for the DOS Games Jam. As such, although it is a new game, it very much has the feel of a puzzle game created back in the early 90's. The object is to escape the tower, with the aid of your AI entity; you can switch back and forth between the human protagonist and the AI at any time, and you'll need the abilities of both to get through all of the rooms. It plays well and looks good so give it a try and support the author if you like it! (Source code in C++ is included in the ZIP file.)

title: CD-Man
description: One of the earliest (and most famous) attempts to modernize the classic Pacman game. As with most Pac-Man type games, there is no real story, just collect the pellets and avoid the enemies. This variant features wonderfully drawn EGA graphics, innovative gameplay elements (gates & keys) and it generally plays very well. Each stage has its own surprises! (The version listed here is v1.5 which most people will likely remember, with the Pac-Man looking main character and only 2.5 finished levels. There is also a v2.0 with a different main character and more levels, but the legality of distributing that version is questionable.) Video ReviewVideo review of CD-Man, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Amulets & Armor
description: Amulets & Armor is an interesting first-person perspective RPG game that unfortunately never got much attention, presumably due to failed publishing and marketing efforts. The game attempts to combine the best elements of FPS games and RPGs, and to some degree it succeeds, having passable graphics and sounds, along with a variety of gameplay options and even multiplayer. However the game also has design problems and bugs, so it is at best a flawed unknown classic. (Note that as of 2013 the full version has been released for free as a 80meg download, see the official site to download it.) Video ReviewVideo review of Amulets & Armor, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Alien Carnage

This game features great graphics and awesome SB sound effects and music. The gameplay is very shooting oriented, similar to Duke Nukem. You also collect money to buy new weapons from vending machines. Very cool, and Apogee (now 3D Realms) has recently released the entire full version of this game as freeware! Click below to download the full version. Video ReviewVideo review of Alien Carnage, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Stargunner
description: Stargunner is a little known shooting game (shoot em up) from Apogee, publishers of other great games like Commander Keen, Duke Nukem and (related by genre to Stargunner) Raptor: Call of the Shadows. Stargunner is a bit more simplistic than Raptor, but generally its no less fun to play, and includes decent low-res VGA graphics and booming sound effects. Levels are repetitious but that's somewhat expected from the genre. Overall its a well made shooter for fans of space shooting games along the lines of Gradius or Raiden. (This game has been released as freeware! Enjoy! Note that it's a large file, approx 40MB!) Video ReviewVideo review of Stargunner, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: System Shock
description: System Shock was a revolutionary and memorable game that is hard to place in a single genre. It does use a 3D FPS engine similar to other games like DOOM, but it also includes puzzle and RPG elements. The documentation included with the game states: "System Shock is not meant to be DOOM. System Shock is a RPG game for one player only, just like Ultima Underworld, not a multiplayer action game like DOOM." So there you have it, straight from the developers, or perhaps some marketing person, we don't really know. In any case, in System Shock you play a hacker who is trying to stop SHODAN, a futuristic AI gone berserk, from destroying the Earth. The game is immersive as it draws players into its creepy atmosphere. Definitely an influential game that inspired later story-intensive first-person games such as Deux Ex. (This demo version contains the first level of the game.)

title: Banyon Wars
description: Banyon Wars seems to be an earlier version of the more well-known Soleau Software game Isle Wars. The object of both games is, like the board game Risk, take over the map by warring with competing armies. You must distribute your troops and decide when to attack. Random events can alter the game as well. You play against two computer-controlled opponents (no multiplayer) in glorious CGA color, and there are seven difficulty levels to choose from. Not a bad game of its type, although the aforementioned Isle Wars is probably a better choice.

title: ZZT
description: Before Epic Games (creators of the Unreal series and now the mega-hit Fortnite) even became known as Epic Megagames, Tim Sweeney created this relatively simple GCS which served as the inspiration for Megazeux and resulted in over 100,000 registrations by users. That's not too shabby. It was the level editor which captured peoples' imaginations. Even though ZZT was eclipsed by Megazeux in terms of usability, features, graphics, sound, etc., it is somewhat popular. Also, thousands of ZZT games have been created, and many are available on the net! And dozens of those are actually good! ;) Just kidding, people have made a lot of amazing stuff with ZZT over the last over 30 (!) years! Note: Even though the game says 'Registered Version: Do not distribute', Epic released the registered version for free. The DOSBOX_ version also includes a sampling of user-created worlds made in ZZT. Download thousands of games and read much more about ZZT and its history at Museum of ZZT. Video ReviewVideo review of ZZT, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Arcy 2
description: Arcy 2 is an puzzle / action game where the object is to collect all of the keys on the level and get to the exit. Your smiley-face character needs no more storyline or motivation other than that! Similarly to the Lolo series of games, the enemies you will encounter move predictably, so although you will sometimes need quick reflexes, thinking and planning ahead are more important. The graphics and SFX are minimal but they get the job done. Thankfully the in-game help (push F1) explains what all of the different symbols are. (This game was originally shareware but has been released for free by its publisher. All three games are available in the archive, although only the first is playable online.)

title: Capture the Flag
description: This game was given several glowing reviews upon its initial release (1994/95) and its easy to see why. This shareware game has an interface that is very professionally done and rivals the commercial games of its time. The graphics are clean and functional, and overall the game is very well designed. This is a clever turn-based strategy game where the object is to capture the other team's flag. Multiplayer play is supported, via hotseat (same computer), modem or PBEM (Play By EMail).

title: Aethra Chronicles: Volume One - Celystra's Bane
description: The Aethra Chronicles is an in-depth roleplaying game where you build a party of three adventurers (somewhat painstakingly so with all the different options) before venturing out on your epic quest! You can also acquire hired helpers during the game, for a maximum party of six heroes! This RPG was apparently based on the real-world Rolemaster pen-and-paper RPGs, which helps explain its depth. The presentation of the game is good, with detailed graphics and MIDI music, although the music repeats rather frequently. The gameplay is classic PC RPG type stuff, with certain elements borrowed from the SSI "Gold Box" series of games. Definitely not a game to play casually, but if you're looking for an in-depth long-term investment, this might be your game. (Probably download and play offline if that's the case ...)

title: Gobliiins
description: This demo version of the full game provides a brief glimpse into the humorous and entertaining adventure game Gobliiins, the first of a series of games. In the game you control three goblins (gobliiins?) each with a unique ability. In order to solve the puzzles, you will need to experiment and use each of their abilities: One uses items, another has great strength (punches things), and the third uses magic. The graphics and animation are great here (the memorable intro cutscene sets the tone), as are the sound effects, although there is no music. Great fun to play, although this demo version is limited, it gives you a glimpse into what you can expect in the full game.

title: Sokoban 3D
description: Sokoban 3D is an interesting idea for a game that just doesn't work well in practice. Sokoban of course is the classic block-pushing game of which there are many variations. The goal is to push all of the blocks onto the markers. Blocks can only be pushed, not pulled, and only one block may be pushed at a time. This version is in 3D, which makes it very difficult to visualize the layout of the level, and even to know exactly where you're standing in relation to the blocks. There is a map mode if you hit Tab but you can't move in that mode. It's probably more fun to play another non-3D Sokoban game, the novelty of 3D wears off quite quickly.

title: ADOM Ancient Domains of Mystery
description: If you enjoy Roguelike games, you'll want to try ADOM. (Its full name is "Ancient Domains of Mystery".) It features primitive ASCII graphics (like most Roguelikes) but it is very in-depth, even more so than Nethack. The game takes place not only in dungeons, but on the overworld and in towns as well. It is constantly being updated, so you may want to visit the ADOM homepage to check for new versions. There is now a full graphical updated version available on GOG.com.

The engine and most of the enemies, powerups, etc are the same, except with all new level designs. Since the basic game is the same, if you enjoy the other Keen games, you'll probably like this one. title: Castle Adventure
description: This is a very old "graphic" adventure game which uses textmode / ASCII characters. Despite its simplicity, there is something charming about its gameplay, and it is nostalgically remembered by gamers who played it in the DOS era. Many adventure games back in 1985 were still text based, so having any kind of visual representation would no doubt be welcomed. Anyways, the game itself is rather average, but it does include action and adventure elements, although there is very little plot. It plays sort of like a Kroz-type ASCII game mixed with a text adventure. A modern Windows remake is available here by Chris Benshoof and is likely a better way to play this game these days!

title: Micro's Dilemma II
description: Micro's Dilemma II is the sequel to the original Micro game, however it was released several years before the Micro! Deluxe game. The gameplay is similar to the other games in the series, albeit with not as refined graphics, UI, and gameplay as the Deluxe version. The goal is still to cause the laser to pass through all of the spheres; you do so by aligning mirrors to reflect the laser as well as using any of the other objects on the playing field. There is some decent puzzle action here, although as mentioned the deluxe version above is probably a better choice.

title: Klass of 99
description: Klass of 99 is a remake / update of a classic ZX Spectrum Skool Daze and Back To Skool games from the 1980's. You play as Eric, a troublemaker who is on a quest to delete his permanent record from his school's computer. In order to do so, you'll need to help him get onto the headmaster's computer without getting caught too many times by the teachers. The graphics and sounds have received significant upgrades from the original, and the pixel art is well drawn and quite charming. The game controls well, although the multiple different buttons are hard to remember. Also if you've never played the original you'll likely have no idea what to do at first; see the beginner's help guide for some tips to get you started!

title: Moraff's World
description: Moraff's World is one of several first-person RPG dungeon crawling games released by Moraffware in the early 90's. There really is no story to consider, so the entirety of the game is exploring various dungeon and dungeon-like areas to kill monsters (over 40 different kinds) and collect items. Like other Moraff games you're presented with a plethora of different graphical options upon running the game but which one you select won't have much impact on the game itself. I found it somewhat disorienting having the four different views, but I suppose it helps to be able to see your surroundings. If you're a fan of first-person dungeon crawlers check it out, otherwise, there's not much here for you ...

title: Action Supercross
description: Action Supercross (it's now called "Elasto Mania" in more recent Windows versions) is a motorbike simulation game that lets you drive your motorbike around a bunch of fun levels, bouncing and crashing into stuff. It features nice graphics, realistic physics, and the ability to create your own new content for the game. In fact many people seem to enjoy creating new levels, graphics etc for this game, as evidenced by the fan sites that are/were popular online. Now there are even two pseudo-sequels for Windows and an iOS app, all using the "Elasto Mania" name. The physics model may or may not be as accurate as claimed; it's definitely not an arcade racer, and you will likely crash often! (Fun fact: This game was referenced in an XKCD comic!)

title: POD
description: POD is a simple puzzle game where the object is to traverse over all of the tiles on the board without falling off. (No relation to the UBI Soft game released in 1997!) Tiles disappear after you step off them, so you'll need to plan your route carefully. However you can't wait too long, because there's a timer counting down as well! Some tiles also need to be stepped on multiple times before they disappear: Green require two steps, cyan require three. And purple tiles will warp you to another place in the level. There are 20 levels included in the shareware version. The graphics are basic but clean and effective. Probably fun if you enjoy puzzle games.

description: Screamer is a 3D perspective arcade-style racing game. By arcade-style I mean that it is not particularly realistic but it does move fast and feature big crashes. The full game has a bunch of car options and tracks to select, but here you can just admire the graphics (non-3D accelerator) and sounds. It runs fairly smoothly so should be good for racing game fans.

title: Commander Keen: Keen Dreams
description: Keen Dreams is sometimes referred to as Keen 3.5, because it was made between the first trilogy of Keen games and Commander Keen 4: Secret of the Oracle. Originally published by Softdisk as a commercially released game, at some point they also made a shareware version. This game plays in some ways like an early test game for what would become the next series of Keen games. Unlike the other games where you have a blaster and pogo stick, here you collect stones (?) which you throw at various food-related enemies in order to stun them. The gameplay is quite similar to the later games, and the graphics are similar too (although more simplistic). Most disturbing perhaps is the fact that there is no music (at least in the shareware release) even though there is a menu option for it! (Apparently it was removed in order to fit the game onto a 360k floppy disk!) Still enjoyable to play however.

title: Snack Attack!
description: Snack Attack! is a Pac-Man clone. While not 100% finished, and intended as a demo of the author's Euphoria programming language book / course, it is still quite playable. It includes the typical Pac-Man intro music and sound effects, and four quirky ghosts that chase you around the maze. The ghosts do appear to move intelligently, although I'm not an expert so I don't know if they move in the same patterns as the original arcade game. Overall it's not a bad version of Pac-Man, although there are better clones available.

title: Hank's Quest: Victim of Society
description: Hank's Quest: Victim of Society is described by the authors as being "A whole new adventure-game in that 'Classic Sierra Style' we all came to love so dearly". Well since it seems to use the actual Sierra AGI engine, it should resemble the old Sierra adventures quite strongly! Your quest in this game as the titular Hank is to host a party at your parents' house. You begin the game without much direction and need to figure out what to do and where to go. The graphics are in the same style as the authentic Sierra games and look quite good. The music is apparently ripped from other games (it's credited to Al Lowe). Generally seems like a fun time if you like the early graphical adventure games.

title: Terroid
description: Ready to shoot stuff? In space? Yep. That's what happens in Terroid. It's a classic R-Type style shooting game where you shoot other ships and pick up powerups. Some parts of this game are a bit strange though. Like why is your ship so big? What do the powerups actually do (most don't seem to do anything)? Why is the music so terrible? Fans of the genre, or classic game competionists, may want to check it out. But it's not a high point in the genre's history. One interesting note is that if you choose "Informations" in the menu you're given a multi-screen backstory for the game, which is often missing from shmups.

title: Mario Teaches Typing
description: If you were a kid with a PC but no Super Nintendo Entertainment System back in 1992 (or even the original NES) it may have been exciting to hear that there were some official Mario games coming to PC! Unfortunately they were "edutainment" games created by Interplay, not by Nintendo themselves. Mario Teaches Typing is at least upfront about what it is. The game does LOOK like a Mario game with colorful graphics and well known characters like Mario, Luigi, Peach, and Toad making appearances. And it does attempt to teach you typing through a series of four typing mini games. This demo version seems to only include the first of these mini games, "Mario's Smash & Dash", whereas the full version also includes "Mario's Wet World Challenge", "Mario's Tunnel Of Doom", and "Mario's Expert Express", all of which are likely less fun than they sound. The program does seem to keep track of the player's statistics and allows for multiple profiles.

description: Digital League Baseball is a baseball simulation game, meaning that you get to manage the team but don't actually get to play. You choose your team, determine the starting lineup, and make substitutions during the game. Other than that, you watch as the computer generates random numbers and compares them against the stats of the players. This game has a graphical view that shows the field, and animations when things are happening, so that's a nice touch given how old the game is. It also includes all of the actual teams and players from the time (no doubt unlicensed from the MLBPA) so that's also pretty neat.

title: Yendorian Tales: Book 1
description: Yendorian Tales is an in-depth party based isometric perspective RPG, a "fantasy role playing game, similar to the Ultima series" as described in the included documentation. You begin by creating a party, choosing each character's class, portrait, and rolling some stats. Then you assemble your party and head out into the world! The interface offers both keyboard and mouse-driven input, however I didn't find it very intuitive, with small icons that aren't immediately obvious. There doesn't seem to be an in-game help feature either. However the game does seem quite professionally put together with a large amount of depth and content, so if you're a fan of the classic CRPG Ultima style game you may want to check this out.

The shareware version of this game offers four tracks to race, against the clock or against multiple CPU opponents. (The full version allows competition for two players simultaneously.) Tracks contain a bunch of different obstacles, like jumps, bridges, oil slicks, holes, etc. The game looks good and plays decently enough, although the controls are difficult to get used to; your car moves too fast and/or turns too slowly, at least that's how I experienced it

title: Amazon: Guardians of Eden
description: Amazon is a graphical point-and-click adventure game using a similar engine to that seen in later Sierra and Lucasarts releases. This demo version allows you to get an idea of what the full (and apparently NOT AT ALL CHILDREN FRIENDLY) game is like. (One of the first things that will happen when you start playing is your character getting shot in the head. Fun times!) The production values are a bit cringe-worthy now but at the time having even short video clips and sound bites was pretty cool. (It also used Access Software's REALSOUND technology to play sounds through the PC speaker if you didn't have a sound card.) According to online reviews it's a decent adventure game if you can overlook a few design flaws.

title: AsciiQuest
description: AsciiQuest is a game creation system (referred to in the docs as an "ascii game creation package") that I honestly haven't invested much time in learning. You can in theory create your own adventure, RPG, and puzzle games, using a collection of tools contained within the game. The game itself uses ASCII characters in Mode 13H, so you have access to 256 colors. This gives the games a unique look, but it also limits your visual options. Compared to something like ZZT, this GCS seems more difficult to learn. There is a character editor and even a music editor where you enter notes on an ASCII piano! Included in the zip file is a 20 page Microsoft Word .DOC file included to explain how things work, but it would be a challenge to get a working game running on this today since as far as I know there is no community support available. Still, an interesting and mostly unknown GCS.

description: Barren Planet is a modern DOS game created in CGA graphics mode. A series of battles is linked together to form the full campaign, with the outcome of one battle determining what battle is fought next." You will probably want to read the Barren Planet Manual (PDF) to learn how to play!

title: Hexen: Beyond Heretic
description: The sequel to the popular Heretic game, Hexen takes the Heretic engine and adds some notable improvements, like weather effects, breakable environments, roleplaying elements and less linear gameplay. Instead of just playing through levels, you must venture through the "hub" which connects various worlds. The atmosphere created in this game is well done, and if you're a fan of early 3D shooting games chances are you'll enjoy this 4-level DEMO version of Hexen.
multiplayer: Up to 8 players, LAN, Modem, Coop, Deathmatch, Internet

title: Hopy-ONE
description: Hopy-ONE (or in some places at least, "Cyborg Hopy-ONE") is a strange single-screen platformer game. You control your robot, which has unique ways of moving around the screen. It has an awkward jump, and also these tendrils that you can extend to keep you in the air and then move around horizontally. It's about as awkward as it sounds when I try to describe it. On each level you must collect all the orbs then make it to the exit, or one of multiple exits. Graphics are decent but sounds effects are repetitive and get old fast. Definitely unique but not something I would personally want to play.

title: Bolo Adventures I
description: Bolo Adventures is an EGA puzzle game which feels much in line with other Soleau Software puzzle games. This game is one of the many variants of Sokoban, where the main object is to push blocks around to escape each level / screen. There have been many additions to the gameplay to add more variety to the levels, such as different kinds of pushable blocks, enemies, and obstacles like lasers and water. (Rescue Rover came to mind for some reason while playing Bolo Adventures, probably due to the lasers.) Graphically the game is rather plain with simple EGA sprites to depict each object. There are 20 levels in this shareware version versus the 40 in total that you get in the registered version.

title: BrainStorm Pro
description: BrainStorm Pro is a gravity-based piece-matching game which bears similarity in its gameplay to the Epic Megagames classic game Brix. Both seem inspired by Taito's Puzznic game, although Brix was an obvious clone / rip-off, whereas BrainStorm Pro has its own style while retaining similar gameplay. The goal is to match up all the pieces, using your mouse to click and drag them as they fall downwards. Different environmental blocks can affect how your other blocks move or exhibit their own unique properties to deal with. A decent game with 20 levels available in the shareware version.

title: Rooms of the Abyss
description: Rooms of the Abyss is a basic first-person perspective dungeon crawling game. Your quest is to ... well there's a long story in the MANUAL.TXT file (which you may want to look at anyways for gameplay controls / tips) but it doesn't really matter. You need to wander through the dungeons, slaying monsters, finding keys, and unlocking doors until you find your way to the next level. There is an automap feature which is nice. However the combat seems pretty basic and uninteresting. The graphics draw slowly using basic shapes, so the gameplay proceeds slowly as well. Also, it took me a few moments to realize that the left and right arrows actually make your character STRAFE and not TURN, so you can't actually TURN AROUND in this game. You just go forward, back, and side to side! Weird. One of the authors has released the full version for free and so you can download / play the registered version here.

description: CoffeeBreak Card Games is a shareware game that is probably a bit too limited to entice people to spend the $30US (approximately $55US in today's money!) to buy the full game, despite the decent production values displayed here. The shareware version includes two card games: 52 Pickup and Crazy 8s. Both play decently enough, and thankfully there is a bit more strategy to 52 Pickup than the version my dad had me play back in the day! In any case, the other four games are only available upon registration, which is unfortunately no longer possible. You may want to also check out other card games on DOSGames.com.

title: Sir Addalot's "Mini" Math Adventure
description: Sir Addalot is a children's math game. The goal is to stop the evil dragon Scorch from terrorizing the kingdom. To do so, you, brave Sir Addalot, must match equal mathematical expressions, as knights of old often did. The game has decent graphics, as well as PC speaker "music" (you may want to turn it off in the options menu). Keyboard and mouse controls are provided. The game generally plays well, although the action the player takes is identical throughout the entire game, even though you move to different "castles" you still do the exact same thing. There are difficulty levels however so once a child starts getting bored you could turn up the challenge. (Bonus: See a scan of the magazine ad for this game courtesy of Mobygames!)

title: Dynamo Draughts
description: Draughts (aka "Checkers") is a strategy-based board game for two players. The object is to collect all of your opponents' pieces by jumping over them. This computerized version contains playing options, including adjustable board sizes from tiny 4x4 up to larger-than-usual 10x10. It includes three built-in settings: USA Pool, International, and Spanish, although you can customize it yourself. Strangely there doesn't seem to be a two-player option, so you must play against the computer, and there are no difficulty settings. There are a lot of other things though, like records of all the moves, saving / loading a game, etc. It uses the "WINDOS" system to simulate a Windows-like look in DOS.

It includes three built-in settings: USA Pool, International, and Spanish, although you can customize it yourself. Strangely there doesn't seem to be a two-player option, so you must play against the computer, and there are no difficulty settings. There are a lot of other things though, like records of all the moves, saving / loading a game, etc. It uses the "WINDOS" system to simulate a Windows-like look in DOS.
sources.title: Dynamo Draughts

title: 3D Xmas Adventure: Santa's Rescue
description: Spread the holiday cheer with this mediocre somewhat-Christmas themed game! It was released by Pie in the Sky Software to promote their 3D game creation system. As such, it's a decent game made with it, but it's still not great. There is a story in the game but it's not too important. You're running around outside in a forest with a lot of trees. A candy cane is your only weapon (?!) and you have to pick up Christmas stockings which work as ammo (?!?!). The original website describes it like this: "Armed with a magic candy cane that shoots jingles and sprinkles, you run around the North Pole gathering gifts, freeing grounded reindeer, and thawing out elves. Beware of the growling abominable snowmen and the menacing grinchy creatures!" Generally it looks and sounds okay, and as with all Pie in the Sky 3D games, it plays a bit too twitchy. It's not obvious what you're supposed to do or where to go, or even which characters are enemies.

title: Jason Jupiter, Star Cadet, In 'Unfinished Business'
description: Unlike the first game in the Jason Jupiter series, which is a platformer, this sequel is a Boulderdash-like game. The object is to collect the required number of borxidium (heart-shaped symbols) and then make it to the exit, while avoiding monsters and falling rocks. There are actual graphics this time (CGA sprites) instead of the text-mode characters used in the first game. Levels span multiple screens, and unlike the first game, you don't need to collect EVERY heart to progress, only the required number displayed at the bottom of the screen. It also includes an editor to edit the game's levels!

title: Outburst - The Game of Topics
description: Outburst is a board game, originally developed in 1986, that seems similar to the still-popular Family Feud game show. A topic/category is shown, and the participant(s) must guess the top answers related to that topic. This text-mode DOS version allows two players to go head-to-head, or allows a single player to challenge the computer with varying difficulty settings. A sample topic is "PARTS OF A TACO" of which includes the shell, cheese, meat, etc. The game works pretty well, although it shows you the topic before the timer starts with an opportunity to pass, which allows you unlimited time to think of answers before starting the timer, so the timer is basically useless.

title: Magus
description: Magus is a roleplaying game created by Ronny Wester, better known for his Cyberdogs and C-Dogs action games. This, however, is a somewhat small-scale and comical turn-based RPG. You begin by creating your party, which includes the usual character types (such as barbarian and wizard) and not-so common types (duck and duck wizard). Then you proceed to move each member of your party in turn around the map, collecting treasure and fighting enemies. It can be somewhat tedious to move each character, and there's really no plot. However, the graphics have an endearing quality to them, and there is some random humor in the game that helps keep things interesting.

title: Absence
description: Absence is a mod (total conversion, I would say) of Wolfenstein 3D. After id Software released the Wolf3D source code, many people made their own maps, mods, and full conversions, of which Absence is recognized as being ground-breaking and worthwhile within the community. It of course include new levels, a new storyline, new graphics and sounds (although many are ripped from other games like DOOM) and the addition of new features not found in Wolf3D, such as finding written notes, or acquiring items from walls. If you enjoy Wolf3D you will likely also enjoy this game. (Note: The yellow keycard in the first level is tough to find but keep searching, you'll find it eventually! It's location is a seeeecret ...)

title: Sokoball of Osaka
description: Sokoball of Osaka is, as you might expect, a version of the classic Sokoban block-pushing puzzle game. This version has the same goal (get all of the blocks to the target(s), here they are "exit shafts") but also includes other kinds of tiles, like one-way tiles and levels that change their layout when a certain tile is stepped on. The gameplay generally works well, although the graphical style make distinguishing the different tiles a bit difficult. A total of 18 puzzles are included in the shareware version along with an editor to create your own puzzles. The included puzzles are all rather difficult so this game will be a good choice if you're looking for a challenge.

description: This is the graphical version of the original Wanderer game; the original was made by Steve Shipway in 1988. See the extra files for the original ASCII version. Like the original text-mode game, Wanderer is a Boulderdash derivative where the object is to collect the diamonds and avoid the hazards before making your way to the exit. There are many different obstacles here and you will need some careful planning, and likely some trial and error, to beat all of the levels.

LOOK carefully and GET ready to play this fairly typical but professionally done adventure game. Check the official hint guide (PDF) if you get stuck. (This game was originally a commercial game but was released for free by its original authors.)

title: Aqua Man
description: Aqua Man is yet another puzzle game from that master of puzzles, William Soleau of Soleau Software! (Some of which seem quite similar to each other yet are nonetheless different ...) Aqua Man is no longer mentioned on his website, which may be due it's name, which is identical to the popular DC comic character, although of course the game itself is unrelated. The game involves pushing blocks around to complete an unbroken line from the starting tile to the ending tile. Level 1 seems rather difficult, so don't expect any hand-holding easy levels to get you started! There is a level select though so you can try out other levels.

title: Descent II
description: The sequel to the awesome original Descent game, this game picks up right where the first left off. You again fly your ship with full range of movement around the many mine shafts destroying enemy robots. There are of course new enemies to fight and new features like the Guide-bot. The engine used seems the same engine used in the original game with some minor additions, but the graphics look a little better and it still plays quite well and runs smoothly ... at least in DOSBox, not sure about hardware back when it was released in 1996! A great game and worthy sequel, despite the sometimes motion-sickness inducing movements. There are three levels to try in this demo version. title: Final Impact
description: Final Impact is a game that possesses most of the qualities necessary for a hit game, with great production values, sound effects, and slick design. However, it unfortunately falls a bit short in the gameplay department. It's a mission-based shooting game with a similar format to Raptor, where you fly missions and earn money to buy new weapons and upgrades. The actual missions seem VERY difficult, and the way your ship fires (depending on the weapon, you can fire in 4 or 8 directions) is not easy to do. The default controls also probably will need to be reconfigured but thankfully you can do that within the game. Seems like a bit more playtesting would have made this game great, but as-is this demo is a great example of the kind of production values of this period of time. (Full game was released on CD with a full soundtrack.)
multiplayer: Up to 2 players, Simultaneous shared keyboard cooperative

title: Attack of the Petscii Robots
description: It may appear that Attack of the Petscii Robots is an action game at first glance, but it's more of a strategic game with some action elements. The goal is to destroy all of the robots in the level. To do so, first you'll need to search around and find some weapons and items. Then you'll have to use them carefully in order to defeat all the baddies. It offers numerous graphic modes to choose from and some AdLib based music. It's a fun and charming game. Definitely a unique experience, although I personally found the constant "searching" mechanic to get a bit tiresome. title: Stone Mist
description: Stone Mist is a classic early Ultima style RPG, complete with turn-based battles and a fairly in-depth character generation system (that must be run separately before running the game). The story is typical fantasy RPG fare, and there are some quirks to the engine, but overall it's a competently presented game with decent VGA graphics. There is an extensive documentation file (SMVOL1.DOC) that you will likely need to reference since the in-game help is minimal. I didn't make it too far into this game but there seems to be a decently large world to explore, and at least you can (usually?) run from battles if you don't want to fight monsters constantly. (Note: The DOSBox version playable online defaults to a sample character I made; download and run the game on your own computer to create your own.)

title: Black Hole
description: Black Hole is a timed puzzle game where the object is to clear all of the tiles off the screen by walking on them. According to its author Terry Cavanagh (yes, that one) it's based on a game called POD. The game is presented well and it seems like there are a lot of levels and a lot of variations on the basic gameplay which are gradually introduced as you play. The difficulty spikes up pretty rapidly with the fourth level already providing a decent challenge, especially since each level is also timed. Source code (QuickBasic) and a level editor are included. Consider buying Terry's excellent VVVVVV game and/or Terry's Other Games pack for more of his work.

title: Menace of Dr Spoil Sport
description: Oh no! Dr Spoil Sport plans to destroy the Earth with his super laser on his floating space station! Only YOU can stop him by teleporting there and disabling this fiendish weapon! So in this "virtual reality" game (created using the Virtual Reality Studio software) you run (or slowly stumble your way through) a simulated 3D-ish environment and click on things to try to get to the next area. Like most Virtual Reality Studio engine games, it's a bit awkward to navigate around, and knowing what to do takes a lot of trial and error. There is some shooting, but the gameplay actually has more puzzle-solving and exploration than action. However there is an attempt here to do something interesting with the engine, so if you have the patience to battle the user interface you may enjoy this.

title: Blupi at Home
description: Blupi at Home (the character is also sometimes referred to as Eggbert in English-speaking countries) is a game based around the French character Blupi. It's a game primarily for young children (3-8 are the recommended ages) based primarily around exploration. You use the mouse to click things around Blupi's house, and he will perform some action with them and also spell out the word for you to read. There are some minigames to discover as well. It's sort of charming but I doubt that most kids who are old enough to confidently use the mouse in the way necessary to play this would be too interested in it. This game was originally released commercially but has since been made freely available by its developers in 2017. Visit the official Blupi website here for more free Blupi games. Thanks goes to Mr Fibble of DOS Games Archive for preparing this re-pack which works easily in DOSBox.

title: BombAway
description: BombAway is similar to Tank Wars, Scorched Earth, and all of the rest of the turn-based artillery-firing games. Set your angle and velocity, and hope you are able to dial it in before your opponent does! This game is two-player only, and lacks some of the bells and whistles that later games provided. You must hit your opponent RIGHT in the CENTER of their tank in order for your shot to count, so it may look like you hit your opponent, but you'll need to adjust your settings ever so slightly to actually make it count.
multiplayer: Up to 2 players, Turn-based shared keyboard and/or mouse

title: Double Pacman
description: Double Pacman is a well-done rendition of the arcade classic game with the added feature of offering two-player simultaneous play. The game looks very similar to the original, and offers both cooperative and competitive modes of play. As expected, you eat dots, collect power pellets, and avoid ghosts. If you have a second player (and can stand sharing the keyboard with them) the game takes on a whole other level of gameplay. The game was made in 1994 but seems to have only been released recently by its author, and the Turbo Pascal 5 source code is also available from the author.
multiplayer: Up to 2 players, Simultaneous shared keyboard cooperative or competitive

description: 2048 is a simple but well made text-mode game that is exactly what you probably expect: A version of the popular 2048 mobile puzzle game. The object is to smush numbered blocks of the same value together to progressively increase their value, doubling each time, until you reach the mythical 2048. Here the game is presented in colorful ANSI-like style with intuitive WASD keys for shifting the pieces. You can restart to begin a new game, and your progress is automatically saved when you quit.

title: Kaboom
description: Kaboom is not a variant of the classic Atari 2600 game Kaboom. (If you're looking for that, try Kerboom! which is a decent DOS clone.) Anyways, this game is a deathmatch fighting game for up to four players. At least two human combatants are required, otherwise it'll be rather boring since there are no CPU opponents available. (This is apparently a public beta version so it's missing some features the author planned for the full game.) There are no weapons other than the default blaster, so you'll need to use that (and avoid all of the other things trying to kill you) to take out your opponents as you fly around the gritty industrial type arenas. It looks good and controls well, and there are plenty of options to tinker with, but the core gameplay won't likely hold your attention for too long, especially if you don't have a second player around to play with.
multiplayer: Up to 4 players, Simultaneous shared keyboard competitive deathmatch

title: Chesshousers
description: Chesshousers is an interesting and visually eye-catching puzzle game. The goal is to direct your player (a glove) through an isometic-perspective maze. You have no weapons, all you can do is move around and push/destroy certain objects. Chess pieces move as the do in the chess board game (ex, pawns move straight ahead) and you'll need to carefully think through their movement before you push them to progress. The graphics look great but the isometric viewpoint sometimes makes it unnecessarily difficult to see what's going on. (There is a helpful list of objects in the game and what they do on the Mobygames description.)

Other than that it's pretty solid as a whole although no particular part is very remarkable.

title: DBQuest
description: DBQuest is seemingly the most well-known game created using the DCGames game creation system. It is an RPG that includes 256-color graphics and a large world to explore, with 75 NPCs to talk with and a large number of areas to traverse. You begin at your own home, and quickly find the castle nearby with the king & queen inside, who give you a quest to find an amulet to save their ill son. Typical RPG fare. Monsters are visible on the map, where you also fight them without transitioning to a separate battle screen. The graphics align pretty closely to the Ultima games.

You are tasked with protecting your comrade troops, first by shooting enemy soldiers in windows, then by shooting down enemy missiles and planes "Missile Command"-style.
